newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trend weak in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trend weak in early trading.

text.p: Stocks opened weaker on Wednesday, as investors cautiously awaited corporate earnings results and the Wall Street's next move, brokers said.
"We expect the index to trade in a narrow range of 11,150 to 11,250 in a wait-and-see attitude, said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities Ltd.
The Hang Seng trended down 28 points to 11,195 on lower turnover of around HK$400 million in the first 30 minutes of trading.
Brokers said investors were awaiting results from the Henderson group, due out later on Wednesday.
"The Henderson results will indicate the trend of the market," Lai said.
Major blue chips Henderson Land and Henderson Investment as well as newly listed subsidiary Henderson China will report earnings for the full year ended June 30 on Wednesday.
"I think people expect very good results," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at G.K. Goh Securities.
Property shares were leading the market down, after having been the best performing sector in the previous three sessions.
The commercial and industrial sector, however, managed a positive opening, rising 0.15 percent. CITIC Pacific led the sector with a gain of HK$0.20 to HK$33.60.
Henderson Land dropped HK$0.50 to HK$61.25 after advancing strongly to a new record high of HK$62.25 on Tuesday.

Henderson Investment shed HK$0.10 to HK$8.10, while Henderson China was untraded at HK$16.50. The shares, which were offered at HK$21.50 in March, have fallen sharply and now appear to be good value, said another broker.
China Light and Power advanced HK$0.60, or 1.82 percent, to HK$33.50 to make it one of the best performing shares.

Hopewell's Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) was also active, rising HK$0.35, or 2.36 percent, to HK$15.20. "The share is expensive at more than 20 times 1996 earnings, but the full commissioning of Shajiao C has given the price some support," said Geoffrey Cheng, research analyst at Standard Chartered Securities.
Road King Infrastructure came in for profit-taking. The issue lost HK$0.25, or 3.9 percent, to HK$6.15.
